findings.summary: The low-bound update uses `lo = mid` instead of `lo = mid + 1`, causing an infinite loop in the binary search.
findings.failure_scenario: Call search_insert([1,3,5], 4). Iterations: lo=0,hi=3,mid=1,arr[1]=3<4 -> lo=1; lo=1,hi=3,mid=2,arr[2]=5>=4 -> hi=2; lo=1,hi=2,mid=1,arr[1]=3<4 -> lo=1 (unchanged). Now lo=1,hi=2 repeats forever because mid==lo and lo never advances, so the loop never terminates (hangs). Whenever the two-element window has arr[mid] < target, the search spins indefinitely.

findings.summary: Binary search updates lo = mid instead of lo = mid + 1, causing an infinite loop when the target belongs after mid.
findings.failure_scenario: Call search_insert([1, 3], 5). Iteration: lo=0,hi=2 -> mid=1, arr[1]=3<5 so lo=1. Next: lo=1,hi=2 -> mid=1, arr[1]=3<5 so lo=1 again. mid never advances because mid==lo, so lo < hi stays true forever and the function hangs. Any target larger than an element at the low half of the current window triggers this. Correct code must set lo = mid + 1.

findings.summary: The lower-bound update `lo = mid` fails to advance past mid, causing an infinite loop when arr[mid] < target and mid == lo.
findings.failure_scenario: Call search_insert([1, 3], 5). Iteration 1: lo=0, hi=2, mid=1, arr[1]=3<5 so lo=1. Iteration 2: lo=1, hi=2, mid=(1+2)//2=1, arr[1]=3<5 so lo=1 again — lo never changes, hi never changes, and the `lo < hi` condition stays true forever. The function hangs (infinite loop) instead of returning 2. Correct code should be `lo = mid + 1`.
